claims.statement: GitHub webhook deliveries use POST /webhooks/github: the route verifies X-Hub-Signature-256, records deliveries, ignores unsupported event types/actions, applies workspace routing, returns 503 when workspace ownership cannot be read so GitHub retries, and schedules accepted handlers as FastAPI background tasks.

Automatic review for PR opened/ready_for_review and push watch processing is gated by is_repo_auto_review_enabled; enabled-review repositories are opt-in and the backing-store lookup fails soft as disabled.
process_github_pr_ready skips draft auto-review unless the PR author's review_draft_prs profile override, or the owning workspace default when no override exists, enables draft reviews.

Explicit PR review requests flow through trigger_pr_review_from_ref: it fetches PR metadata, ensures the canonical reviewer thread, persists PR/head metadata with watch=True, posts a review-started comment, dispatches the reviewer graph, and stores its run ID; request_pr_review parses a GitHub URL and delegates to it, as does the dashboard re-review endpoint.

reviewer_thread_id(owner, repo, pr_number) is UUIDv5 over '{owner}/{repo}/pr/{pr_number}/reviewer'; its formula is a cross-process persisted-data routing contract, so changing it orphans live reviewer state.

Reviewer runs are dispatched with assistant_id='reviewer', mapped to agent.graphs.reviewer:traced_reviewer_agent, and store_current_reviewer_run_id saves a returned run_id in reviewer thread metadata.

Findings are durable PostgreSQL records under a PR, linked to the reviewer thread by pull_request_finding_state; first access migrates legacy thread-metadata findings once, while thread metadata retains reviewer operational state such as PR identity, heads, and watch.
coerce_finding normalizes legacy flat and nested GitHub publication identities into canonical comment/thread ID lists and a forward-only surface_state, so callers work with one finding shape.

Findings writes use locked database read-modify-write: mutate_findings locks PR finding state and persists only changed mutations, replace_findings merges snapshots by ID, and append_finding de-duplicates by fingerprint among open findings.
When a reviewer thread backing findings storage is absent, the storage layer raises ReviewerThreadMissingError and tools return thread_not_found with an explicit do-not-retry instruction.

add_finding validates generated title and enums, normalizes one-ended ranges, rejects out-of-diff anchors with success:false and in_diff:false, and accepts file-level findings although they have no inline GitHub payload.
add_finding drops suggestions longer than MAX_SUGGESTION_LINES (four) while retaining a description-only finding and returning a warning.

Finding publication requires open findings at or above the severity threshold, defaulting to medium; ranking takes precedence over fallback severity/file/line ordering, and confidence is recorded but does not gate publication.

publish_review reconciles live PR review threads, excludes previously commented findings and, on re-review, findings not first seen at the live head; it posts one GitHub PR review containing marker-bearing inline comments and a marker-bearing summary.

publish_review resolves the live head SHA from reviewer-thread metadata rather than a frozen config, then records review and marker-mapped comment identities in a merged findings write to support later reconciliation and avoid duplicate publication.

publish_review treats unresolved-anchor 422 responses as repairable once by dropping identifiable invalid anchors and retrying the remaining batch; eval publication is dry-run, while an empty already-reviewed PR resolves fixed threads and advances last_reviewed_sha without another summary.
PR lifecycle events toggle reviewer watch: closed disables it, reopened enables it, and converted_to_draft disables it only when the author's effective draft-review setting is off.

A watched push dispatches a re-review only when an open PR has a reviewer thread, watch is enabled, the head differs from last_reviewed_sha, and the diff changed; an unchanged diff advances last_reviewed_sha and creates then settles a visible success check on the new head.

Changed-push re-reviews reconcile threads, persist the live head, create a fresh check, and dispatch with re_review=True and a prompt to reconcile existing findings and add net-new ones; ready_for_review skips dispatch when the current head already equals last_reviewed_sha.

reconcile_findings_with_review_threads matches findings by embedded marker before stored identity, backfills publication identity, records the newest non-bot reply as an interaction needing reassessment, and resolves an open finding only when all matched threads are resolved; it persists only on change.

A non-bot reply to an Open SWE review comment is routed ahead of ordinary mention handling; its handler reconciles, associates the parent comment to a finding, stores a needs_reassessment interaction, and dispatches a reviewer_event='finding_reply' run.

Automatic first-review and changed-push paths create and track an Open SWE Review check; replacing a check settles superseded checks as neutral where possible, and settlement clears review_check_run_id only after a successful completion PATCH while retaining a pending result on failure.

The after-agent settle_review_check_on_exit middleware closes a tracked un-published review check as neutral, but retries review_check_pending_result when publication completed and only the completion PATCH failed.

Focused reviewer tests cover auto-review admission and token scoping, watched-push and check behavior, PostgreSQL findings migration/mutation/order, tool anchor and resolution validation, publication behavior, and reconciliation.

Reviewer preparation treats PR descriptions and existing review-thread bodies as untrusted, XML-delimited data with closing tags neutralized; the reviewer prompt also incorporates workspace/repository/base-commit guidance while preparation makes a failed or unavailable walkthrough non-blocking.

PrepareReviewerRunMiddleware prepares a replaceable per-thread sandbox and checkout, materializes a first-review or re-review diff, and computes per-file/per-side changed lines; it optionally waits only a bounded period for a same-head review-scout walkthrough and proceeds without one when unavailable.
